newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia 1997 corn imports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 1997 corn imports seen rising.

text.p: Indonesia is expected to import about one million tonnes of corn in 1997, compared with 800,000-900,000 tonnes in 1996, Budiarto Soebijanto, chairman of the Federation of Feedmeal Producers said on Wednesday.
"Corn imports this year are expected to be about one million tonnes compared with 800,000-900,000 tonnes last year," he told Reuters on the fringes of an international conference on food.
He said 500,000 tonnes of corn had been imported so far this year, adding that a similar amount was expected to be imported through the rest of 1997.
"The actual import numbers would depend on the local corn harvest in the second semester of this year," he said.
Soebijanto said there would be a significant decline in corn imports next year if domestic corn production increased.
"The government has set a target of planting 500,000 hectares with hybrid corn this year, which could raise production by an additional 1.5 million tonnes," he said.
He said, however, although there has been some progress in the planting of hybrid corn it had not been satisfactory.
Soebijanto said he did not have details on how much of the 500,000 hectares had been planted with the high-yielding corn.
